ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which Arabic word means "good morning (the reply)"? (1 mark)
   A. السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ
   B. إِصْبَعٌ
   C. نَظِيفٌ
   D. صَبَاحُ النُّورِ

2. Which reason best explains why we greet one another? (1 mark)
   A. It shows respect and kindness to the person we meet
   B. It is only needed when we meet strangers
   C. It is only needed at school
   D. It is only needed by adults

3. How would a girl say 'I am a pupil'? (1 mark)
   A. anaa tilmiidha
   B. anaa tilmiidh
   C. ismii tilmiidh
   D. haadhaa tilmiidh

4. What does the Arabic word خَلْفَ (khalfa) mean? (1 mark)
   A. beside
   B. above
   C. under
   D. behind

5. Which Arabic word means "chair"? (1 mark)
   A. سَرِيرٌ
   B. غُرْفَةٌ
   C. حَدِيقَةٌ
   D. كُرْسِيٌّ

6. What does the Arabic word تَفَضَّلْ (tafaddal) mean? (1 mark)
   A. gift
   B. drink
   C. juice
   D. please, go ahead

7. What does the Arabic word خُضَارٌ (khudaar) mean? (1 mark)
   A. fish
   B. vegetables
   C. bananas
   D. bread

8. How is the Arabic word أَغْلِقِ الْبَابَ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. aghmiD ʿaynayka
   B. ukhruj
   C. aghliqi l-baab
   D. uktub

9. Which Arabic word means "open the door"? (1 mark)
   A. اُخْرُجْ
   B. افْتَحِ الْبَابَ
   C. أَغْمِضْ عَيْنَيْكَ
   D. قِفْ

10. What does the Arabic sentence أَنَا أَرَى بِعَيْنِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I smell with my nose.
   B. I speak with my mouth.
   C. I see with my eye.
   D. I hear with my ear.

11. What does the Arabic word رِيحٌ (riih) mean? (1 mark)
   A. environment
   B. cold
   C. beautiful
   D. wind

12. What does the Arabic sentence نُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْبِيئَةِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The weather is cold.
   B. The weather is rainy.
   C. We look after the environment.
   D. The weather is hot.

13. How do you read the syllable بُو? (1 mark)
   A. tu
   B. ti
   C. buu
   D. na

14. Which sound does the Arabic letter ش make? (1 mark)
   A. k as in kite
   B. kh, a throat sound like the ch in loch
   C. t as in tap
   D. sh as in shop

15. How do you read the syllable بَ? (1 mark)
   A. bu
   B. sa
   C. ba
   D. bii

16. How do you read the shadda in the word jad-dun? (1 mark)
   A. The letter is silent
   B. The letter daal is said twice
   C. The vowel is long
   D. The word is a question

17. How is the Arabic word قَلَمٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. sahn
   B. taawila
   C. qalam
   D. kuub

18. Which Arabic word means "Saturday"? (1 mark)
   A. الْجُمُعَةُ
   B. السَّبْتُ
   C. الْيَوْمَ
   D. الْأَرْبِعَاءُ

19. Which Arabic word means "hand"? (1 mark)
   A. رَأْسٌ
   B. لِسَانٌ
   C. وَجْهٌ
   D. يَدٌ

20. What does qawiyy mean? (1 mark)
   A. hot
   B. small
   C. strong
   D. new

21. What is a thematic word? (1 mark)
   A. A word in English
   B. A very long word
   C. A number
   D. A word that belongs to the theme of a text

22. How is the Arabic word تَحْتَ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ʿinda
   B. fii
   C. taHta
   D. amaama

23. What does the Arabic sentence الْكُرْسِيُّ عِنْدَ الْبَابِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. Do not play with the knife.
   B. The key is in the cupboard.
   C. The chair is at the door.
   D. I like bananas.

24. What is the difference between ف (faa) and ق (qaaf)? (1 mark)
   A. faa has a dot below
   B. faa has one dot above and qaaf has two dots above
   C. They have no dots
   D. faa has two dots above and qaaf has one

25. What is the name of the Arabic letter ب? (1 mark)
   A. siin
   B. baa
   C. dhaal
   D. Haa

26. What is the name of the Arabic letter ع? (1 mark)
   A. alif
   B. kaaf
   C. ʿayn
   D. Saad

27. What is the ending of the letter ة in جَدَّةٌ called? (1 mark)
   A. taa marbuta
   B. shadda
   C. hamza
   D. sukuun

28. What does the Arabic sentence الْبَابُ كَبِيرٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The table is small.
   B. The door is big.
   C. The chair is new.
   D. The window is clean.

29. What does the Arabic word ذُرَةٌ (dhura) mean? (1 mark)
   A. fish
   B. maize
   C. chicken
   D. fruit

30. Which sentence is a good ending for a paragraph about your room? (1 mark)
   A. fii l-ghurfati sariir
   B. uhibbu ghurfatii
   C. haadhihi ghurfatii
   D. al-kitaabu ʿalaa t-taawila

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give three rules for a handwriting contest. (3 marks) (3 marks)

32. Translate into English: aakulu l-aruzza (2 marks)

33. Explain how the same Arabic word can look different but keep its meaning. (2 marks) (2 marks)

34. Translate into English: al-maa'u nadhiif (2 marks)

35. Write in Arabic sounds and translate: 'I eat bread and I drink milk.' (2 marks) (2 marks)

36. Describe three steps of making a weather poster. (3 marks) (3 marks)

37. Translate into English: ayna l-kitaab? (2 marks)

38. Write one Arabic sentence about your body in sounds and translate it. (2 marks) (2 marks)

39. Translate into English: al-baabu kabiir (2 marks)

40. Translate into English: ashrabu l-maa'a (2 marks)

41. Translate into English: al-maa'u mufiid (2 marks)

42. Translate into English: anaa araa biʿaynii and atakallamu bi-famii. (2 marks) (2 marks)

43. Explain how the voice should sound in a statement and in a question. (2 marks) (2 marks)

44. Explain why untidy handwriting can be a problem in Arabic. (2 marks) (2 marks)

45. Describe how to carry out a dictation of the days of the week in pairs. (3 marks) (3 marks)

46. Translate into English: fii baytii matbakh (2 marks)

47. Translate into English: anaa araa biʿaynii (2 marks)

48. Translate into English: haadhaa jismii (2 marks)

49. Translate into English: shukran li-istimaaʿikum (2 marks)

50. Translate into English: fii l-ghurfati sariir (2 marks)

51. Name three rooms of the house in Arabic (English letters) with meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

52. Write four weather words in Arabic sounds with meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — صَبَاحُ النُّورِ
   صَبَاحُ النُّورِ (sabaahu n-nuur) means good morning (the reply).

2. A — It shows respect and kindness to the person we meet
   A greeting is for everyone. It shows that we see and respect the other person.

3. A — anaa tilmiidha
   A girl uses tilmiidha, with the ending -a. A boy says tilmiidh.

4. D — behind
   خَلْفَ (khalfa) means behind.

5. D — كُرْسِيٌّ
   كُرْسِيٌّ (kursii) means chair.

6. D — please, go ahead
   تَفَضَّلْ (tafaddal) means please, go ahead.

7. B — vegetables
   خُضَارٌ (khudaar) means vegetables.

8. C — aghliqi l-baab
   أَغْلِقِ الْبَابَ is read aghliqi l-baab and means close the door.

9. B — افْتَحِ الْبَابَ
   افْتَحِ الْبَابَ (iftahi l-baab) means open the door.

10. C — I see with my eye.
   أَنَا أَرَى بِعَيْنِي (anaa araa biʿaynii) means: I see with my eye.

11. D — wind
   رِيحٌ (riih) means wind.

12. C — We look after the environment.
   نُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْبِيئَةِ (nuhaafidhu ʿalaa l-bii'a) means: We look after the environment.

13. C — buu
   بُو is read buu.

14. D — sh as in shop
   The letter ش makes the sound sh as in shop.

15. C — ba
   بَ is read ba.

16. B — The letter daal is said twice
   A shadda doubles the letter, so jadd has two d sounds.

17. C — qalam
   قَلَمٌ is read qalam and means pen.

18. B — السَّبْتُ
   السَّبْتُ (as-sabt) means Saturday.

19. D — يَدٌ
   يَدٌ (yad) means hand.

20. C — strong
   qawiyy means strong.

21. D — A word that belongs to the theme of a text
   Thematic words belong to the main topic of a text.

22. C — taHta
   تَحْتَ is read taHta and means under.

23. C — The chair is at the door.
   الْكُرْسِيُّ عِنْدَ الْبَابِ (al-kursiyyu ʿinda l-baab) means: The chair is at the door.

24. B — faa has one dot above and qaaf has two dots above
   Only the dots separate these two letters.

25. B — baa
   The letter ب is called baa.

26. C — ʿayn
   The letter ع is called ʿayn.

27. A — taa marbuta
   ة is taa marbuta and appears at the end of many feminine words.

28. B — The door is big.
   الْبَابُ كَبِيرٌ (al-baabu kabiir) means: The door is big.

29. B — maize
   ذُرَةٌ (dhura) means maize.

30. B — uhibbu ghurfatii
   uhibbu ghurfatii (I like my room) gives a closing feeling.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone writes the same words for the same time; judges look at shape, size, spacing and neatness; everyone is encouraged and praised.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible rule.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: I eat rice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: In different writing styles the letter shapes change a little, but the letters, sounds and meaning stay the same.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for shapes change and 1 mark for meaning stays the same.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: The water is clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: aakulu l-khubza wa ashrabu l-haliiba. I eat bread and I drink milk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the Arabic sounds and 1 mark for the translation.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Draw and colour the sun, clouds, rain and wind; write the Arabic word under each; add a sentence and a title and display it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Where is the book?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example aktubu bi-yadii. I write with my hand.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct sentence and 1 mark for the translation.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: The door is big.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: I drink water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Water is useful (good for you).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: I see with my eye. I speak with my mouth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each translation.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: In a statement the voice falls at the end. In a question it rises at the end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Letters that differ only by dots may look the same, so the reader may read the wrong word.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dots and 1 mark for the wrong reading.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: One learner says a day; the other repeats it, says the sounds and writes the letters from right to left; they check and correct together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying the day, 1 mark for writing and 1 mark for checking.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: In my house there is a kitchen.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: I see with my eye.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Thank you for listening.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: In the room there is a bed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example ghurfa (room), matbakh (kitchen), hammaam (bathroom), hadiiqa (garden).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning, up to 3.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example shams (sun), matar (rain), riih (wind), sahaab (clouds).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.
